'''Mickaël Gelabale''' (born May 22, 1983) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Élan Chalon]] of the [[LNB Pro B|Pro B]]. He also represents the [[France national basketball team]] internationally. Standing at {{height|m=2.01}}, he plays either at the [[small forward]] position or the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position in a [[Small ball (basketball)|small ball]] configuration.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sbnation.com/2014/3/28/5555120/nba-player-smell-marcin-gortat-brandon-rush | title=Who is the smelliest player in the NBA? | date=28 March 2014 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Gelabale started playing professionally with [[Cholet Basket]], averaging 10 points and five [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game in his final season (2003–04). Subsequently, he joined [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], being used in the side's rotation during two seasons (about 23 minutes per game combined).

At the end of [[2004–05 ACB season|his first season]], Gelabale was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the second round (48th overall) of the [[2005 NBA draft]], but opted to stay in [[Madrid|the Spanish capital]] instead of immediately joining the NBA.

On July 12, 2006, he signed a two-year contract with the Sonics, joining [[Johan Petro]] as the second French player on the team. Stuck on the depth chart behind both [[Ray Allen]] and [[Rashard Lewis]] (in [[2006-07 NBA season|2006–07]]) and [[rookie]] [[Kevin Durant]] ([[2007-08 NBA season|2007–08]]), Gelabale appeared sparingly for the team, tearing his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] midway through his second year.

On March 29, 2009, he resumed playing, one year after his injury, with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] in the NBA [[D-League]].

On September 28, 2009, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the NBA signed him to their practice squad to give him a chance at a long-term contract, but he was waived on October 10, 2009, two weeks before the beginning of the 2009–10 regular season. He then signed with [[Cholet Basket]] in the [[France|French]] [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball|Pro A]] on November 26, 2009.<ref name="Gelabale Mickael"/> He won the 2009–2010 [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball|Pro A]] championship and was named [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the Play-Offs Final with [[Cholet Basket|Cholet]].

In July 2010, Gelabale signed a contract with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]].<ref name="Gelabale Mickael">[http://www.lnb.fr/index.php?pid=9&id=A65099&from=2009&type=1 Gelabale Mickael] {{in lang|fr}}</ref><ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73376/180/asvel-basket-lands-mickael-gelabale-davon-jefferson Asvel Basket lands Mickael Gelabale, Davon Jefferson]</ref>

In August 2011 he signed with [[Spirou Basket]] in [[Belgium]] for one year,<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/87129/180 Spirou Charleroi signs forward Gelabale]</ref> but his contract was later indefinitely suspended because of an injury.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/31540/mickael_gelabale_leaves_spirou_charleroi.html Mickael Gelabale leaves Spirou Charleroi]</ref>

In January 2012 he signed with [[BC Khimki|Khimki Moscow]] until the end of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/34058/khimki_officially_signs_mickael_gelabale.html Khimki officially signs Mickael Gelabale]</ref>

In August 2012 he signed with [[KK Cedevita]].<ref>[https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/basketball.aspx?NewsID=285823 Cedevita lands Mickael Gelabale]</ref> After the Croatian team was eliminated in the [[EuroLeague]], Gelabale signed with [[Valencia Basket]] in December 2012.<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=90039 Gelabale, presented in Valencia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130811052856/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=90039 |date=2013-08-11 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref>

On January 19, 2013, he signed a ten-day contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-mickael-gelebale-10-day-contract Wolves Sign Mickael Gelabale To 10-Day Contract]</ref> On January 29, 2013, he was signed to a second 10-day contract.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-mickael-gelabale-2nd-10-day-contract Wolves Sign Mickael Gelabale To 2nd 10-Day Contract]</ref> On February 8, 2013, he signed with the Timberwolves for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/johnson-gelabale-stay-rest-season Johnson, Gelabale To Stay For Rest Of Season]</ref> Gelabale was waived by the Timberwolves on July 7, 2013.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-greg-stiemsma-and-mickael-gelabale Timberwolves Waive Greg Stiemsma and Mickael Gelabale]</ref>

On July 31, 2013, Gelabale signed a one-year contract with his former team [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].<ref>{{cite web|title=MICKAEL GELABALE IS BACK TO BC KHIMKI|url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2013/july/957/|work=en.bckhimki.ru|access-date=31 July 2013}}</ref>

On November 21, 2014, Gelabale signed a one-month contract with [[SIG Basket|Strasbourg IG]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/142055/mickael-gelabale-signs-with-sig-strasbourg.html Mickael Gelabale signs with SIG Strasbourg]</ref> After his contract expired, he left Strasbourg.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/146581/sig-strasbourg-mickael-gelabale-part-ways.html SIG Strasbourg, Mickael Gelabale part ways]</ref> On January 5, 2015, he signed with [[Limoges CSP]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/147463/mickael-gelabale-moves-to-limoges.html Mickael Gelabale moves to Limoges]</ref>

On July 2, 2015, he signed a two-year contract with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans Sarthe]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/166787/mickael-gelabale-signs-with-le-mans.html Mickael Gelabale signs with Le Mans]</ref>

On October 10, 2017, he signed with [[Élan Chalon]].<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/249455/elan-chalon-signs-mickael-gelabale.html Elan Chalon signs Mickael Gelabale]</ref> He averaged 11.1 points and 5 rebounds per game in 2019–20. In June 2020, Gelabale extended his contract until 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mickael Gelebale extends with Elan Chalon |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/mickael-gelebale-extends-with-elan-chalon/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 4, 2020 |date=June 4, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

==French national team==
In September 2005, Gelabale helped the senior men's [[France national basketball team|French national team]] to the [[bronze medal]] at the [[EuroBasket 2005]]. In [[EuroBasket 2011]], his team won the silver medal, and in [[EuroBasket 2013]], they won the gold medal.
